key_insight: Language models can continuously improve themselves by extracting and reusing transferable knowledge from their real-world interactions, enabling on-the-fly learning during deployment rather than relying solely on offline annotated datasets.
problem_solved: Overcomes the gap where rich deployment experience (user interactions, mistakes, corrections) is ignored by traditional offline training pipelines, preventing models from adapting and improving from live usage.
method: Extract transferable experiential knowledge from interaction trajectories (user queries, model responses, corrections) to form compact, reusable units of experience.
Accumulate and organize these experience units into an evolving repository or memory that captures recurrent patterns, failure modes, and successful strategies.
Apply lightweight online updates or retrieval-guided adaptation so the model uses accumulated experience to improve performance continuously during deployment.
impact: Enables lower-cost, continual improvement of LLMs using real deployment data, improving robustness, personalization, and responsiveness while reducing dependence on expensive offline annotation cycles.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: Interaction → Experience Extraction → Experience Repository → Online Model Update
Timeline or curve chart illustrating model performance improving over deployment time as experiences accumulate
Schematic of an experience unit (e.g., user query + model response + correction) feeding into a memory bank
Icons representing users, model, storage/memory, and a refresh/loop symbol to denote continuous learning
paper_title: Online Experiential Learning for Language Models
paper_authors: Tianzhu Ye, Li Dong, Qingxiu Dong, Xun Wu, Shaohan Huang
